news.title: New coach Xavi promises Netherlands new energy after poor World Cup
news.lede: Soccer Football - Netherlands unveil Xavi Hernandez as new coach - KNVB Campus, Zeist, Netherlands - August 25, 2026 Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez poses with the kit announcing his new contract REUTERS/Piroschka Van De Wouw. AMSTERDAM, Aug 25 - Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez is promising an attractive style of football but more importantly a desire to win during his tenure with the national team. The former Barcelona midfield great and later coach has signed a four-year deal through the next World Cup and promised he would look to inject new energy into the Dutch, who were eliminated in the last 32 at this year's finals. “We have many talented players, but the most important thing for me is to create a team, a group and football-wise we want to create a very brave team to dominate the game, to take the initiative with the ball,” he told a press conference on Tuesday.

news.title: Rising Market Values of World Cup 2026 Stars Deepen Italy’s Sorrow
news.lede: Only three players from Serie A and just one Italian are in the top 50 most valuable players worldwide following a World Cup transfer update. Italy’s failure to reach the World Cup final for the third consecutive time has had significant sporting and financial consequences. Specialised football website Transfermarkt has updated all players’ values after the World Cup, and Sandro Tonali is the only Italian player included in the top 50, ranking 46th. There’s concern for Serie A as well, given that the only representatives from Italy’s top flight in the top-50 ranking are Lautaro Martinez, Kenan Yildiz and Nico Paz.

news.title: Iraq Retains Graham Arnold After Historic World Cup Return
news.lede: Graham Arnold has extended his Iraq coaching contract through the 2027 Asian Cup after guiding the Iraqi national team back to the World Cup after 40 years. ERBIL (Kurdistan24) - Graham Arnold has extended his contract as Iraq's national football coach through the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, choosing a six-month renewal after guiding the country back to the FIFA World Cup for the first time in four decades. The 63-year-old former Australia coach said the Iraq Football Association had offered him a four-year agreement, but he opted for the shorter extension as the national team turns its attention from this summer's World Cup to the Gulf Cup and Asian Cup. "I have renewed my contract for six months and this decision is in my best interest and in the best interest of the Iraq national team," Arnold told a news conference in Baghdad on Monday, according to The Associated Press.

news.title: Kurt Okraku Hails Black Stars’ Progress Despite World Cup Exit
news.lede: Ghana Football Association (GFA) President Kurt Okraku has praised the Black Stars for their resilience and progress at the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico. Ghana advanced to the second round of the tournament after a commendable group-stage campaign against some of the strongest teams in world football before their journey was ended by Colombia. Although the Black Stars had ambitions of progressing further in the competition, Okraku believes their performance offered positive indications about the direction of the national team. “The Black Stars demonstrated resilience and promise at the 2026 World Cup in the USA, Canada and Mexico,” Okraku said.

news.title: ‘We will be silent no more’: former international players call for change at Fifa
news.lede: A group of former international players, including World Cup winners and Fifa legends, called on Monday for immediate change at world football’s governing body, saying its leadership under embattled president Gianni Infantino had been blinded by power. Infantino has been under mounting pressure to resign after shelving his proposal to create a commercial body for Fifa tournament rights and sell off 20 per cent to private investors. “We share the exact same ⁠concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” said former players including France’s 1998 men’s World Cup winners Emmanuel ‌Petit, Bixente Lizarazu and Robert Pires as well as American former women’s world champion Briana Scurry and former England international Lucy Bronze. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift ‌away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership.

news.title: Lego sales jump 21% to nearly £5bn, helped by World Cup and F1 ranges
news.lede: Lego sales have risen by more than a fifth as tie-ups with the football World Cup, Formula One and the hit film KPop Demon Hunters as well as its flower-based and Star Wars kits drive demand. The toymaker said its revenues had increased by 21% to 41.9bn Danish kroner (£4.8bn) in the first six months of 2026, driven by strong growth in the Americas, Europe and the Asia-Pacific regions, offsetting stalled sales in China. Sales by its clients to consumers rose by 22% as it produced World Cup kits, including mini figures of players such as Harry Kane and even building kits of superstar players, including Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi which were retailing for up to £159.99. Net profit increased 32% to 8.6bn Danish kroner (£1bn) as the group launched 330 new products including its hi-tech Smart Play kit, with bricks that emit sounds and light.

news.title: John Swinney launches £500k World Cup fund to 'back Scotland's future football stars'
news.lede: JOHN Swinney has launched a £500,000 World Cup fund to "support Scotland's future football stars". The First Minister launched the fund during a visit to Scotland's national stadium, Hampden Park in Glasgow, on Tuesday. It comes following the success of Steve Clarke's team at the Fifa World Cup in June, with the Scotland men's team qualifying for the tournament for the first time since 1998. Lawrence Shankland celebrates during win over Denmark at Hampden Park in November, in which Scotland qualified for the World Cup (Image: PA).
